raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrate bilateral, ill-defined opacities that are predominantly located in the lower lung zones (basal predominance) and appear more extensive on the right side. This radiographic pattern is characteristic of Acute Fibrinous and Organizing Pneumonia (AFOP), distinguishing it from the apical distribution of edema or the upper lobe predominance of PCP.
